messages:
morgan: Heads-up: seeing steady memory drift in KV cache during very long contexts (~100k tokens). Not allocation spikes — looks like fragmentation + poor reuse. p99 token latency up ~8% during some cycles. dumping allocator stats and perf samples.
jun: can you paste alloc stats / a mini repro? :thinking:
morgan: here's a quick allocator snapshot from the long-run perf job (2h):
```
KVAllocator:
  total_slabs: 128
  used_bytes: 42300312448
  free_bytes: 6200431872
  largest_free_block: 32768
  avg_block_size: 4096
  fragmentation_pct: 21.5
  free_list_reuse_rate: 60%
  uncollected_stale: 180k entries
```
leah: 21% fragmentation is pretty high. are we rounding to power-of-two buckets? what's policy for entries >4k?
morgan: we bucket at 512/1k/2k/4k/8k/16k currently (round-up). many small expired KV entries leave holes inside slabs; cross-slab coalescing doesn't happen so holes persist. reuse rate ~60% but free blocks scattered.
sam: sounds like the root cause is slab-level isolation + no compaction across slabs. compaction reduces mem drift but causes latency spikes. we need a middle ground.
morgan: ran three configs today: no-compact, compact-on-idle (background), and compact-threshold-25%. results: 
```
Run: 2h long-context load (100k tokens)
- no-compact: mem_growth +1.12GB, p99_latency +9ms, throughput stable
- compact-on-idle: mem_growth +200MB, p99_latency spikes during compaction: +40ms (rare)
- threshold-25%: mem_growth +350MB, p99_latency +15ms, compaction freq moderate
CPU overhead (avg): no-compact 3%, compact-on-idle 6%, threshold-25% 4.2%
```
jun: interesting. can we try adaptive compaction: only compact slabs with >50% reclaimable, and do slab-by-slab with small work quanta to flatten latency? also consider tuning small-block family from 4k -> 6k to reduce cross-block waste (tradeoff internal fragmentation).
morgan: prototyped slab-by-slab GC + per-thread freelist transfers. early numbers: reduces p99 spikes ~60%, costs ~+2% CPU. snippet: 
```
for slab in slabs:
  if slab.reclaimable_pct > threshold:
    compact_slab(slab, max_work_units=128)
    yield  # allow other work
```
leah: we should emit per-slab telemetry: reclaimable_pct, compaction_time_ms, post_compact_free_ratio. then canary on dedicated-staging before prod rollout.
infra-bot: deploy bot: starting rollout to dedicated-staging with config: compaction=slab-by-slab, reclaim_threshold=0.5, work_quanta=128
sam: :thumbsup: plan an A/B run vs baseline. collect KV hit/miss, post-compaction fragmentation, latency distributions. ensure cache semantics unchanged (no accidental evicts of warm entries).
morgan: one regression to watch: when compaction runs concurrently with request batching we saw a short stall (~12ms) due to freelist lock contention. possible fixes: sharded freelists or lock-free transfer.
jun: sharded freelists + transfer handoff would probably remove the contention. also benchmark block sizes: 4k vs 6k vs 8k to measure avg wasted bytes per entry and p99 latency.
morgan: action items:
- run canary A/B overnight on dedicated-staging (morgan)
- add per-slab telemetry + tracing hooks (leah)
- prototype sharded freelists + lockless handoff (jun)
- run blocksize microbench (sam)
I will post flamegraphs + pprof outputs tomorrow morning. thanks all :pray:
